To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) simple subspace regularizers for logistic regression classifiers outperform specialized, recent state-of-the-art methods for few-shot class incremental learning, and (ii) the regularizers can be configured to incorporate background information about the classes to be learned.

(1) simple subspace regularization of the weight vectors for a logistic regression classifier can be used to achieve good performance on few-shot incremental learning; (2) subspace regularization is easy to configure, and can be easily combined with background information about the class to be learned; (3) subspace regularization can achieve state-of-the-art results on few-shot incremental image recognition.
subspace regularizers for few-shot class incremental learning are effective for few-shot incremental image recognition and can be easily adapted to incorporate background knowledge about new classes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose to regularize the weights of a logistic regression model by encouraging the new weights to be close to the spanned space of the old weights, which leads to a better performance on the few-shot incremental learning task.
we present a simple approach that enables ordinary logistic regression classifiers to perform few-shot incremental learning, outperforming specialized, state-of-art approaches.

we introduce the subspace regularizers for few-shot incremental classification and show that the subspace regularized logistic regression can be used as an extremely simple and effective approach for few-shot incremental class learning.

simple geometric regularization schemes can be extremely useful in few-shot incremental learning, and we hope this work inspires further exploration along these lines.
